decisions.reason: The carrier wafer was publicly announced, extends the core thin-wafer-handling business, costs little to maintain, and fits the stated direction toward reusable carriers, so management stays committed to it.

The Cu-interposer was launched at SEMICON Europa as a flagship of the firm's packaging-wafer direction and absorbed substantial development investment, so any weak results would be read as a slow market ramp and the firm would persist.

Wafer Universe is a separately founded brand presented as a flagship, sits close to the established offer and carries low running cost, so the public commitment and its fit with the core business make withdrawal unlikely.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and were not presented as a flagship, which makes them the most vulnerable product, but the R&D already sunk and the hope that slow uptake is temporary favor keeping them a while longer.
